findings.description: Critical: Migration 039 uses the UUID ownership registry only when checking an exact-key collision. After ensuring the target, reconcile lines 226-240 cancel every active row with the same input_data.change_id and a different tuple, without a task-type, marker-label, or ownership-registry predicate; lines 243-248 and submit lines 122-129 likewise clear labels based only on mutable payload and the reserved label. An unowned ordinary issue spoofing a noncanonical projection tuple and reserved labels can therefore be cancelled, have its result overwritten, and lose all labels. The round-7 collision test covers only an unowned row at the target tuple, which returns before these mutations. This contradicts design.md lines 70-74 and the claim that registry ownership is the sole mutation authority.
findings.resolution: When projection_labels is non-null, restrict cancellation and stale-label cleanup to task IDs registered in work_queue_projection_ownership. Retain the legacy broad reconciliation predicate only for projection_labels IS NULL. Add submit and reconcile regressions proving an unowned noncanonical spoof row remains byte-for-byte unchanged.

findings.description: Critical: Migration 039's upgrade seed permanently grants database ownership using only mutable task_type, projection-shaped input_data, and the reserved label. An ordinary keyed issue carrying spoofed projection labels before migration 039 is inserted into work_queue_projection_ownership and subsequently passes the exact-key ownership check, allowing relabeling or terminal reactivation instead of projection_key_collision. IssueService.update and PATCH /issues/{id}/labels permit those labels, while the live spoof regressions insert rows only after all migrations have run. The documented caveat covers ambiguous unlabeled rows but not falsely adopted labeled rows.
findings.resolution: Replace the label-derived automatic seed with a trustworthy provenance/backfill mechanism or a fail-closed operator registration procedure. Add an upgrade test that creates a spoofed labeled keyed issue before applying migration 039 and proves it remains unowned afterward.

findings.description: Critical: apply_outcome_or_escalate records the caller-supplied phase as previous_phase after a failed apply-outcome instead of using the authoritative current_phase loaded from loop-state. A stale caller reporting VALIDATE while durable state is IMPLEMENT causes the phase-mismatch guard to fail, after which the wrapper parks ESCALATE with previous_phase=VALIDATE; an approved resume then skips IMPLEMENT. Existing tests cover a matching first failure and an already-ESCALATE retry, not this mismatch path.
findings.resolution: Read and validate the durable current_phase before mutation and use that value as previous_phase. Keep the caller-supplied phase only in diagnostic history. Add a mismatch regression proving resume returns to the durable phase.

findings.description: Nit: The successful in-process apply_outcome_or_escalate path returns immediately when the writer exits zero and never invokes its supplied queue_projection_fn. The canonical write matrix requires apply-outcome to submit an unchanged-generation replay, and the failure branch does project. A process ending after successful bookkeeping but before the following transition therefore misses the specified repair opportunity.
findings.resolution: On a zero writer result, reload the saved LoopState and invoke _project_saved_state in submit mode when a projection callback is supplied. Add success-path coverage asserting the unchanged generation is projected and structured degradation does not alter the return code.

findings.description: Nit: JSON-schema Antigravity reviews still fail protocol ingestion. The configuration now requests JSON output, but _extract_findings unwraps only a direct findings object or Grok's structuredOutput field. The real Antigravity envelope stores the schema-valid review as JSON text in response; round-7 review-manifest.json lines 8-17 records status SUCCESS as Invalid JSON output, requiring manual out-of-band recovery.
findings.resolution: Teach _extract_findings to recursively parse dict- or string-valued response envelopes and add a regression using the exact preserved round-7 Antigravity envelope.

findings.description: Nit: Runtime request models and the authored OpenAPI still expose different projection-label constraints. OpenAPI defines an ordered tuple whose first item has maxLength 135 and whose second item is a fixed constant, while WorkSubmitRequest and WorkReconcileRequest use one homogeneous maxLength-160 item type for both positions. Consequently runtime model validation accepts first-label lengths 136-160 and arbitrary second labels; only the later service check rejects them. The regression tests only length 161 and therefore does not exercise the mismatch.
findings.resolution: Add position-specific or model-level validation that enforces the ordered canonical pair and semantic equality to projection_key before the handler runs. Test lengths 135, 136, and 160 plus an incorrect second item for both request models.
